question: What microscopic arrangement is characteristic of Staphylococcus species?
explanation: Staphylococcus bacteria divide in multiple planes, which causes them to clump together in irregular shapes that resemble bunches of grapes under the microscope. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which laboratory test result is used to distinguish Staphylococcus from Streptococcus?
explanation: Staphylococcus species produce the catalase enzyme which bubbles when exposed to hydrogen peroxide, whereas streptococci do not, making this test essential for basic differentiation. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which feature primarily separates Staphylococcus aureus from other staphylococcal species?
explanation: Staphylococcus aureus produces the coagulase enzyme, which clots blood plasma and marks it as a more dangerous pathogen compared to coagulase-negative species. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why are coagulase-negative staphylococci usually considered opportunistic rather than primary causes of disease?

options.A: They are completely destroyed by normal human sweat
options.B: They never produce any toxins under any circumstances
options.C: They cannot survive outside a laboratory incubator
options.D: They only cause illness when the immune system is weak or skin barriers are broken

explanation: These bacteria live naturally on normal skin and usually do not cause illness unless they enter the body through surgical sites, catheters, or vulnerable newborn immune systems. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary mode of spreading Staphylococcus within a busy hospital ward?
explanation: Direct hand contact by healthcare personnel is the most common way bacteria transfer between patients in clinical settings. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which postpartum patient has the highest risk of developing a staphylococcal wound infection?

options.A: A woman discharged two hours after a normal delivery
options.B: A woman who had an emergency caesarean section after prolonged labor
options.C: A woman who had a normal vaginal birth at home
options.D: A woman who received routine iron supplements during antenatal care

explanation: Surgical cuts, extended time in the hospital, and prolonged labor significantly increase the chance for bacteria to enter and cause an infection. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h3)

question: How do Staphylococcus bacteria usually enter the breast tissue to cause postpartum mastitis?

options.A: Hormonal changes after delivering the placenta
options.B: Blocked milk ducts from tight bras
options.C: Drinking too much fluid during labor

explanation: Breaks in the skin of the nipple during early breastfeeding provide a direct pathway for skin bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus to enter breast tissue. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h4)

question: How do localized staphylococcal skin abscesses typically present on physical examination?

options.A: Painful, swollen lumps with surrounding redness and pus accumulation
options.B: Painless, dry patches of skin that flake off without inflammation
options.C: Bright red rashes that cover the entire body within hours
options.D: Cold, numb areas of tissue with complete loss of sensation

explanation: Staphylococcal infections trigger an intense inflammatory response, producing pus, localized heat, swelling, and tenderness at the infection site. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the medical term for a bacterial infection of a newborn's umbilical stump?
explanation: Omphalitis is the inflammation and infection of the umbilical cord stump, which can serve as an entry point for bacteria to spread through a newborn's body. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why are newborn babies particularly vulnerable to serious staphylococcal skin conditions?

options.A: They absorb many antibodies through breast milk
options.B: They spend most of their time sleeping in warm cots
options.C: Their skin is delicate and their immune system is still developing
options.D: Their body temperature changes more easily than adult temperature

explanation: An underdeveloped skin barrier combined with an immature immune system allows bacteria to multiply and invade newborn tissues much more easily. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the single most effective action a midwife can take to prevent infections from spreading on the ward?

options.A: Restricting all visitors from the ward

explanation: Regular and proper handwashing or sanitizing by healthcare workers removes transient bacteria and stops pathogens from passing between patients. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why does Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) make routine ward treatment difficult?

options.A: It resists many standard first-line antibiotics
options.B: It only grows on plastic medical devices
options.C: It spreads exclusively through the air
options.D: It cannot be seen under a standard microscope

explanation: MRSA strains have developed resistance to common penicillin-class drugs, requiring clinicians to use alternative and often more complex treatments. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h6)
